svg.aria-label: How to write ാ ര ം: 3 parts, ാ, ര, ം, one after another
svg.title: Writing ാ ര ം
svg.desc: 3 parts written one after another: ാ, ര, ം (malayalam). The parts are in the order the hand writes them, which is not always the order they are typed: a vowel sign written to the left of its consonant comes before it. Each vowel sign is drawn on its own, without the consonant it attaches to. Each part has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that part, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished part, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansMalayalam-Static.ttf. Each part is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the parts are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: ാ: Rodney F. Moag, Malayalam: A University Course and Reference Grammar (University of Texas at Austin South Asia Institute and COERLL, updated April 2018; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), Table III 'How to Write Internal Vowel Symbols', p. xx: movement 1 for ാ, written by hand by Thomas Joseph <https://github.com/matjic/malayalam/blob/7141acd2f310bc8928822a7aec61d1149efa6fa3/docs/assets/images/front-writing-030.jpg>; ര: SPACE Kerala (Melwin Sunny and Shaiju T), Thooval Malayalam alphabet learning tool, formation arrows for ര in data/RA.png: green start, blue turn, red end (GPL-3.0, 2013) <https://github.com/spacekerala/Thooval/blob/87143b560bf5aab43837d9da2cddab9bd59cd391/data/RA.png>; ം: Rodney F. Moag, Malayalam: A University Course and Reference Grammar (University of Texas at Austin South Asia Institute and COERLL, updated April 2018; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), Table III 'How to Write Internal Vowel Symbols', p. xxiv: movement 1 for ം, written by hand by Thomas Joseph <https://github.com/matjic/malayalam/blob/7141acd2f310bc8928822a7aec61d1149efa6fa3/docs/assets/images/front-writing-034.jpg>. Source notes on variation: ാ: Moag's Table III (p. xx) draws it as one movement to the right of the dash that stands for the consonant: from the upper tip clockwise round to the lower tip. Moag's book is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, so only these facts (order, start, direction and end) are cited; no drawing is copied. The page is read from the scan in Mathew Jacob's digital edition (github.com/matjic/malayalam, commit 7141acd), which notes that the numbers mark drawing movements that can belong to one continuous stroke, not pen lifts. Santhosh Thottingal's hand reference curves (gitlab.com/santhoshtr/hand, MIT, 2019), which keep several strokes where a glyph has them, record ാ as one stroke from the upper left to the lower left. The grahyam online-handwriting samples (github.com/bluebottlewize/grahyam, no licence, cited as counts only) keep no pen-up marker, but none of the 44 unique samples jumps between consecutive points the way a lift would; they most often start at the upper left (39 of 44) and end at the lower left (44 of 44). The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Malayalam outline of the sign on its own rather than to Moag's drawing. ര: Thooval's RA.png starts at the left foot (green), climbs clockwise over the top, descends the right side, runs left along the bottom and curls up the inner loop to finish at its top (red). Thooval is a GPL-3.0 teaching tool, so only these facts are cited; no image, path or template point is copied. It asks the learner to keep the pen down to the end of every letter, so its single run is checked against two recorded sources that could have shown a lift. Santhosh Thottingal's hand reference curves (gitlab.com/santhoshtr/hand, MIT, 2019), which keep several strokes where a glyph has them, record ര as one stroke from the lower left to the upper right. The grahyam online-handwriting samples (github.com/bluebottlewize/grahyam, no licence, cited as counts only) keep no pen-up marker, but none of the 31 unique samples jumps between consecutive points the way a lift would; they most often start at the lower left (28 of 31) and end at the upper right (18 of 31). The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Malayalam outline rather than to Thooval's letterforms; in that outline the inner loop's top runs into the right side, so the path ends where they meet. ം: Moag's Table III (p. xxiv) draws it as one movement to the right of the dash that stands for the consonant; in Table II (p. xix) it is movement 9 of അം, after the eight movements of അ. The drawn line starts at the upper left of the ring and runs clockwise, ending with its arrowhead on the left side pointing up. Moag's book is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, so only these facts (order, start, direction and end) are cited; no drawing is copied. The page is read from the scan in Mathew Jacob's digital edition (github.com/matjic/malayalam, commit 7141acd), which notes that the numbers mark drawing movements that can belong to one continuous stroke, not pen lifts. The direction is read from a small arrowhead in the scan, so it is stated with medium-low confidence, and other sources differ: an unlicensed tracing app (sabari596's Malayalam alphabet demo) draws the ring of അം from its top, anticlockwise, and the matching signs of other scripts (KanoAI's Gujarati anusvara, HP Labs India's Devanagari anusvara) mostly run anticlockwise. The ring is separate ink, so the pen lifts after the base to make it. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Malayalam outline of the sign on its own rather than to Moag's drawing; that outline prints an open ring, so the path circles the ring's own centre line.
svg.text: How it is written — 3 parts, one after another
Part 2 of 3 — one unbroken stroke · 3 movements
Part 1: stroke order after Rodney F. Moag, Malayalam: A University Course and Reference Grammar (University of Texas at Austin South Asia Institute and
COERLL, updated April 2018; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), Table III 'How to Write Internal Vowel Symbols', p. xx: movement 1 for ാ, written by hand by Thomas Joseph
Part 2: stroke order after SPACE Kerala (Melwin Sunny and Shaiju T), Thooval Malayalam alphabet learning tool, formation arrows for ര in data/RA.png: green
Part 3: stroke order after Rodney F. Moag, Malayalam: A University Course and Reference Grammar (University of Texas at Austin South Asia Institute and
COERLL, updated April 2018; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), Table III 'How to Write Internal Vowel Symbols', p. xxiv: movement 1 for ം, written by hand by Thomas Joseph
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
